pages.title: Farming
pages.text: This section provides information about $(thing)farming$() in $(item)Simply Journey$().

When used in place of soil, certain plants or crops planted on top of it will periodically receive extra growth stages, exactly as though grown with $(item)Bone Meal$(). $(br2)Additionally, farmland tilled from $(item)Rich Soil$() cannot be trampled. $(br2)Rich Soil Farmland must be watered like any other farmland.

$(item)Stoves$() can be extinguished by using a $(item)water bucket$() on them, or using a $(item)shovel$() on it. $(br2)The player can place raw food on a lit Stove by using the food item on it - up to $(bold)6$().

The player can place raw food on a $(item)Skillet$() by using the food item on it. $(br2)A $(item)Campfire$(), $(item)Stove$(), or $(item)Fire$() must be placed under the Skillet in order to cook items.

Its interface can be opened by pressing the use item button on it. $(br2)A $(item)Campfire$(), $(item)Stove$(), $(item)Magma Block$(), $(item)Lava$() or $(item)Fire$() must be placed under the Cooking Pot in order to cook items.
When the correct tool is used on a valid item, it will be broken down into $(bold)1-4$() different outputs, which are swiped sideways. $(br2)There are a few categories for usages.
When right clicked, a menu will pop up where you can put food inside it. $(br2)Nearby animals will flock to the trough to eat the food within.

A $(item)fish trap$() as a means to passively collect fish at the cost of crops. $(br2)The fish trap must be submerged in a $(thing)water biome$() such as lakes oceans rivers otherwise nothing will be caught.
